chunk_findings.detail: `bug_duplicate` does not validate whether the duplicate bug (`bug`) is already closed by another mechanism (e.g., already closed as invalid or fixed independently) before trying to close it. If `bug` is already closed, `bug_invalid` is called on it again, appending a duplicate resolution event to an already closed bug, which corrupts the event log state and contradicts the docstring's claim that it is refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_duplicate.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: `open_duplicates` treats `duplicate_of` as undirected. The inbound scan is correct (`other` lists `bug` in `duplicate_of`, so `other` is the duplicate). `found |= own.linked("duplicate_of")` then adds the originals this bug claims to duplicate. Given D linked `duplicate_of` O, D still open, and `bug fixed D` (own regression test), the fold lists O. `knowledge.py` then tells the operator to run `bug duplicate O --of D`. After D is `resolution == "fixed"` with a test, `bug_duplicate` accepts that and `bug_invalid`s the original. Links written by `bug_duplicate` itself (`link_record(repo, bug, "duplicate_of", of)`) only need the inbound scan; the outbound union inverts the edge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_duplicate.py:29

data.summary: Several 'pins regenerate --only <recipe>' runs in one item need N serial approvals: each regeneration (and each commit of it) changes the state every other pending approval was bound to, so the rest are refused 'of other state'. Observed with 4 recipes on B-dup-closure (Q70afda0c47, Q77f9b355d5, Q4bb10e4c74 refused after Q4338a16148 was used). Also a rollback (failed post-check) leaves state unchanged but code fixes needed before it invalidate the approval. Suggested fix: approve a recipe list in one approval, or bind to the pre-state of the recipe's own files only (not the whole tree/HEAD). Related: pins regenerate re-records main's drift along with the item's change (golden-snapshots rewrote test_golden_outputs and reporting_pin ambr), so each diff must be hand-audited.
